newsitem.title: USA: Columbia/HCA named in shareholder suit.
newsitem.headline: Columbia/HCA named in shareholder suit.

text.p: The law firm of Kaufman Malchman Kirby & Squire LLP said Wednesday it has filed a shareholder complaint seeking class action status against Columbia/HCA Healthcare Corp and certain directors and officers of the company.

The law firm said it filed the lawsuit on April 9 in the federal court for the Middle District of Tennessee, seeking damages for buyers of Columbia/HCA common stock between February 14, 1996 and March 27, 1997.
The lawsuit alleges that the defendants misrepresented and concealed important information related to the company's financial reports and business practices, the law firm said.
It also alleges that certain officers and directors of the company sold stock during the period at inflated prices.
On April 8, a similar lawsuit was filed against by the law firm of Wechster Harwood Halebian & Feffer LLP.

Nashville, Tenn.-based Columbia/HCA, the nation's largest hospital company, said last month it cooperated with federal agents who searched its El Paso, Texas, facilities in a probe involving what it called "a broad range of records and documents." It said the probe was completed on March 20.
The company did not immediately respond to calls for comment on the suit.
